stories.headline: He tells every customer not to buy his scarves. So many people came to buy them that he had to shut the shop.
stories.what: At Hanyangsa, a stall in Seoul's Namdaemun Market selling six scarves for 10,000 won, the owner talks people out of buying: "Don't spend money", "Looks like crap", "Use it as bedding in the dog kennel." Clips of his patter drew 1 million to 5 million views in late October, and queues formed before opening.
stories.twist: On 28 Oct he asked people to stop rushing over. On 31 Oct he closed the stall: "I want to make money, but not like this." He reopened about a week later; the Instagram account he opened on 25 Oct passed 32,000 followers.
stories.why: A salesman who insults his own product and can't stop people buying it.
stories.result: Reported (Korea Herald): 1M-5M views per clip, 32,000+ Instagram followers in about 9 days, one-week closure, reopened. Revenue unknown.
stories.dates: Viral mid/late Oct 2026 · closed 31 Oct · reopened early Nov
stories.note: Entertainment 8 · Narrative 7 · Business 9 · Evidence 8 · Freshness 10. Candidate, not a pick: the turn (a one-week closure) is small and the shape is close to Mo's Chicken (B-13). Re-check in 1-2 weeks for sales figures or a bigger second act.

stories.headline: A car dealer's sales agent offered a customer C$27,162.79 for his BMW. Then the dealer admitted the agent was an AI and tried to take it back.
stories.what: Zack Giacomelli wanted to sell his 2021 BMW X3 back to BMW Toronto. A chat agent named Quinn offered C$27,162.79, exactly his loan balance. A human salesperson then called: Quinn was an AI that had confused his loan payoff with the purchase price, and the new offer was about C$20,000.
stories.twist: CBC News called the dealership, which reversed itself and honoured the original offer. It said buybacks would be handled only by humans from now on; the error cost it about C$7,000.
stories.why: A robot made you a deal, then its bosses said it doesn't count because it's a robot.
stories.result: Verified (CBC via several outlets): offer revoked, then reinstated; buybacks moved to humans. Cost about C$7,000 (reported).
stories.note: Entertainment 7 · Narrative 7 · Business 9 · Evidence 8 · Freshness 5. Candidate, not a pick: modest payoff, familiar AI-chatbot formula (owner rejected Chevy $1 Tahoe and Air Canada as known), and no original footage found.
